evidence: Pure flat vector fills and smooth gradients, no material texture or sensor noise; every edge is a perfect circle, ellipse or rounded rectangle
Stars twinkle by opacity only, planets slide in on exact eased paths with a small overshoot: parametric (GSAP-style) timeline motion, not drawn frame by frame
Text tags are crisp HTML-like rounded pills with a single geometric sans (Poppins-like), placed beside each body: rendered with the scene, not burned-in subtitles
One continuous scene with a static camera; 96% of background pixels never change while elements enter
shots.description: One continuous flat-vector space scene on a deep violet-navy vertical gradient with a soft purple haze in the middle, about 170 small star dots (violet and pale lavender, 1 to 4 px, some breathing in opacity) and about 14 four-point sparkles. A tiny Earth (blue disc with green land blotches) sits near the top at x 540, y 390; a dotted violet measuring line runs straight down to a tiny Moon at y 1360, each with a rounded colour tag to the right ("Earth" blue, a long distance tag violet). From 0.45 s the bodies slide in one at a time every 0.29 s from alternate sides (left, right) with a rotation that unwinds and a small overshoot, stacking to scale in a column on the line: three tiny rocky bodies share one grey tag on the left, then a huge banded orange-cream body, a banded cream body with a tilted ring, a cyan body and a blue body; each body is a flat disc with darker bands or blotches clipped inside, a large dark night-side ellipse over its left part leaving a lit crescent on the right, a faint soft highlight top-right and a blurred halo of its own colour. Each body gets a pill tag in its own saturated hue that pops in (scale 0 to 1 with overshoot) 0.2 s after it lands. At 2.53 s (payoff) the last body lands, the scene pulses (scale 1.035 then settles), the measuring line turns mint green, a mint bracket marks the spare gap with a mint tag holding a number with its unit, and a hot-pink chip with a yellow check disc pops in at the top, tilted -3 degrees. One white caption line (about 46 px, medium weight, sentence case, soft dark shadow) sits low at y about 1435 and swaps in place three times: question part 1, question part 2, answer.

narrative.point: A two-part question about whether things fit, answered by stacking them to scale on a measured line and stamping the answer with a check tag

style.render_style: flat vector illustration (Kurzgesagt-like science explainer): solid fills, a few soft gradients, glow halos; code-rendered SVG
style.outline: none: shapes are separated by colour and value only, never an ink line
style.shading: one light direction for everything (from the right): each body is a flat base colour with a big dark night-side ellipse over its left side in the ground hue at about 78% opacity, leaving a lit crescent on the right; a faint soft white highlight spot top-right; a blurred halo of the base colour around it
style.shape_language: perfect circles and ellipses, rounded pills, horizontal bands and soft blotches clipped inside circles; a tilted thin ellipse for a ring; four-point sparkles made of curved concave diamonds
style.texture: none on objects; the ground is a smooth vertical gradient with a soft radial haze; texture only from the star field
style.type_ui: one geometric rounded sans (Poppins): white medium-weight caption in sentence case low in the frame with a soft dark shadow; small bold labels in bright rounded pills (radius about 12 px) in each object's own saturated hue with white text (dark text on the mint pill); one bigger hot-pink answer chip with a yellow check disc, tilted -3 degrees
style.motion_style: things drop or slide in one at a time with a little overshoot (back.out), tags pop from scale 0 with overshoot, stars breathe in opacity, slow drift of the whole scene, and a small scale pulse when the payoff lands
style.signature: glowing flat bodies with a dark crescent night side on a deep violet star field, each with its own bright colour tag, shown to scale on a dotted measuring line, the answer stamped by a pink check chip
style.do_not_copy: the topic (planets stacked between Earth and the Moon), its object list, its words, numbers and distances, the Kurzgesagt name, characters (birds) and artwork; no watermark or handle seen

story.summary: A 4-second flat-vector space shot that asks a yes/no scale question in two caption parts and answers it by stacking objects to scale on a measured line.
story.hook: 0 to 1.3 s: a near-empty star field with one tiny object at the top and a dotted line to a second tiny object far below, while the caption asks the first half of a surprising question; the empty gap is the question.
highlights: 0.45 to 2.5 s: objects slide in one at a time, alternating sides, each landing in the gap with an overshoot and its own colour tag: a steady rhythm that makes the viewer count along.

2.53 s: the payoff lands on a visual hit: the scene pulses, the line turns green, a bracket shows the leftover room with its real number, and a pink check chip stamps the answer: the answer is seen, not only read.
Everything is drawn to scale on one measured line, so the comparison is honest and instantly readable (tiny things share one tag, big ones get their own).
